full_judgment: 13. The trial court mainly discussed the evidence at length. While discussing the evidence although he found that plaintiff could not prove his title on the alleged purchase land of 0:84 acres of land, in the land as mentioned in the schedule of the plaint by dint of oral agreement but upon considering the admission of the defendant witnesses he held that plaintiffs is in possession in the suit premises, and thus he decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff. The appellate court, while dismissing the appeal found that the discussion of the trial court is nothing but a mere presumption, which can be held in a suit for partition. But this is a suit for permanent injunction, title is not the main question there to decide which may come incidentally. The possession of the suit land is a prime question to be decided here. Admittedly plaintiff is a co-sharer by inheritance in the suit premises. He further claimed that he has purchased the suit land, from his aunt Sutu Bibi by way of oral agreement. Which was, subsequently not been registered due to of their ignorance. 0.84 decimals of land is mentioned in the schedule of the plaint, which he claim to be his purchased land.
